doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Backing comedians
summary: Playing for comedians such as Pat Cooper with no charts, and a Connie Francis anecdote from Rowe.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What about backing up comedians? That must be a hoot.

That’s fun but you really don’t play that much. You’ll play the opener and sometimes some comedians do sing, and they give you the key, no arrangements, no charts, just play behind them. And once in a while of course the drummer has to be alert with a comedian with these —

The fills and so forth. But you just stay on stage, like with Pat Cooper we would bring him out and he would come out and did his thing and then we’d play him out and you’d have to stay up there the whole forty minutes or an hour.
Yeah, and hear some of the same jokes night after night.
Right, the same jokes. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

I remember playing once with Connie Francis and some guy in the audience said, “We love you Connie.” And we all thought that was such a nice thing. And the next night some guy in the audience goes, “We love you Connie,” it was the same guy.
Like a plant you know. So it’s fun to watch that kind of showbiz.
